messages.subject: MSstats errors
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I was doing analysis using MSstats library but facing many errors with my own data sets as well as with the example data sets (the same data set used in manual).
I am following the workflow with Proteome Discoverer output for DDA provided in the MSstats manual (section 4.5) but just after running (a) " quant <- PDtoMSstatsFormat(raw, annotation=annot) " line it shows multiple warnings.
In the next step of (b) data processing it has shown error.
Am I missing something?
Is there any other data set for which I can re-run the analysis to see if something is wrong with my Proteome Discoverer data sets?

Warning and error messages are as follows-
(a)
There were 50 or more warnings (use warnings() to see the first 50)
> warnings()
Warning messages:
1: In aggregator(Intensity, na.rm = TRUE) :
  no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf
2: In aggregator(Intensity, na.rm = TRUE) :
  no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf

(b)
> cox.progenesis.proposed <- dataProcess(quant,
+                                        normalization='equalizeMedian',
+                                        summaryMethod="TMP",
+                                        cutoffCensored="minFeature",
+                                        censoredInt="NA",
+                                        MBimpute=TRUE,
+                                        maxQuantileforCensored=0.999)
Error in dataProcess(quant, normalization = "equalizeMedian", summaryMethod = "TMP",  :
  unused argument (cutoffCensored = "minFeature")
>

Thanks
Best Regards,

--

Mayank

messages.subject: MSstatsPTM TMT / Label-free mixed input
messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstats Team,
We recently stumbled over the new MSstatsPTM and are very excited as we are increasingly doing more phospho analyses in our facility and would like to also use MSstats for phospho analyses.

Our standard approach usually is to do a phospho enrichment and measure the enriched phospho peptides directly (now with DIA). The flowthrough is collected and labeled with TMT and then also measured.

We therefore end up with a label-free phospho dataset, with protein level information stemming from TMT data.

Is it possible to analyse such data with MSstatsPTM, or are the only options:

label-free PTM input combined with label-free PROTEIN input
or
TMT PTM input combined with TMT PROTEIN input

Again, we would have:
label-free PTM input combined with TMT PROTEIN input.

Best, Klemens

messages.body_plain:
Hi Philipp,

Sorry this took a little longer than expected, I had to make some changes to the converter because it was expecting a different naming convention in the column names of the Phospho (STY)Sites file. I fixed this and now it works with the data you sent over. Just make sure to update the `keyword` parameter as below. I pushed these changes to Bioconductor as a bug fix, but it will take a day or two to propagate in their systems, alternatively feel free to download the package directly from github:

https://github.com/Vitek-Lab/MSstatsPTM

Hope this fixes everything!

Best,
Devon

## Load data
annotation <- read.csv("annotation.csv")
evidence <- read.csv("evidence_red.txt", sep = "\t")

phospho_sites <- read.csv("Phospho (STY)Sites_red.txt", sep = "\t")
prot_groups <- read.csv("proteinGroups_red.txt", sep = "\t")

## Add mod into protein name
test <- MaxQtoMSstatsPTMFormat(phospho_sites, annotation, keyword = "Plex")

messages.subject: Re: MSstatsPTM TMT / Label-free mixed input
messages.body_plain:
Hi Klemens,

On the method side this is definitely something that can be done with MSstatsPTM, however currently the implementation does not have the functionality to handle inputs from differing acquisition methods. I have added this as one of the next major feature enhancements to the package. If you have experiments you want to run through MSstatsPTM in the meantime, it is possible to do this using some of the underlying functions in the package along with the existing code in MSstats and MSstatsTMT. If you'd you like some guidance on how to do this let me know!

Best,
Devon

Best, Klemens

We are looking for volunteers for a usability study of our newly developed UI interface for MSstats and MSstatsTMT. Best,
Devon Kohler

messages.subject: MSStatsTMT adjusted p value
messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstats Team,

I am analyzing a TMT10plex dataset with MSStatsTMT, generated from ProteomeDiscoverer. However, I get same adjusted pvalue on many occasions and none of the proteins have adjusted p< 0.05, however around 600 proteins with p<0.05 in a dataset of 8000 proteins (for one of the comparisons). Is there anything wrong with the scripts below? I am comparing 3 conditions and doing 'pairwise comparison, I have compared with individual 'contrasts' (not pairwise); the result is the same.

input.pd <- PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat(input = raw.pd, annotation = annotation)

quant.pd.msstats <- proteinSummarization(input.pd,
                                         method="msstats",
                                         global_norm=TRUE,
                                         reference_norm=FALSE,
                                         remove_norm_channel = TRUE,
                                         remove_empty_channel = TRUE)

test.pd.pairwise <- groupComparisonTMT(data = quant.pd.msstats,
                                   contrast.matrix = "pairwise",
                                   moderated = TRUE,
                                   adj.method = "BH",
                                   save_fitted_models = TRUE,
                                   use_log_file = TRUE,
                                   verbose = TRUE)

Kind regards,
Sudip
